Learning from Crowds with Crowd-Kit

paper.arxiv.2109.08584

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2109.08584v4. Crowd-Kit methods/governance and benchmark limitations are substantive toolkit research. Inspectedv4 has current JOSS title; originalv1/alternate title rolls into the same arXiv work without crediting unreadv1 science. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The library lacks distributed-cluster execution; M-MSR did not process D_Product in reasonable time and no implementation handled the large binary 3/binary 4 datasets. Its categorical aggregation methods assume one objective true label per task.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Crowd-Kit implements crowdsourced-answer aggregation and learning-from-crowds methods in Python, with pandas/scikit-learn-compatible interfaces and PyTorch modules for direct learning from raw crowd labels.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Categorical evaluation reused four real-world noisy-label datasets and synthetic datasets from prior work; the direct-learning experiments used IMDB reviews and CIFAR-10, with three annotators per object and 100 gold tasks.
